reason: Clean the clogged filter to start restoring airflow to the cooler.
expectation: The repair roll should let me clear the filter cassette for reuse.

alternatives.reason: Comparing the logs may explain the spikes, but I want to start with the physical repair.

effect: The filter is clean, so I can continue rebuilding the air module; the lint alone doesn't justify replacing the compressor.
reaction: The distinction between a clogged filter and compressor failure is useful.
reason: Fit the compatible fan to the cleaned filter to continue restoring airflow.
expectation: The fan cartridge and filter will form a usable air module, though further installation may be needed.

effect: The repaired air module is ready for Rae to fit and check, so I can move on to the cabinet.
reaction: It's satisfying to have the airflow parts assembled.
reason: Fit the repaired module to the isolated cabinet to continue restoring the cooler.
expectation: Rae will fit or check the module in the cabinet; it may still need power and monitoring.

reason: Use the checked service supply to continue restoring the cabinet.
expectation: The cabinet will power up for a service check, though independent monitoring may still be needed.

effect: The cabinet is running again; independent temperature monitoring is the next check.

reason: Attach the independent logger to monitor the running cabinet.
expectation: The logger should record the cabinet's temperature independently; it may take further evidence to interpret the spikes.

alternatives.reason: Comparing the old logs could explain the spikes, but I want to establish monitoring first.

effect: Independent monitoring confirms the cooler held its specified range during the service check; the remaining goal is to investigate the old spikes.
reaction: It's reassuring that the repair was checked independently and storage decisions remain with clinical staff.
reason: Compare the temperature and door-opening logs; this is the only offered combination and may explain the spikes.
expectation: The logs may show whether the spikes coincide with door openings, though that alone might not establish their cause.

effect: Most spikes coincide with door openings, helping explain the air-sensor readings without establishing the temperature of every stored object.
reaction: The distinction between air readings and stored objects is useful.
reason: Give Moth the aligned logs to help interpret the spikes; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: Moth may incorporate the evidence into an explanation, ideally preserving its limitations.

effect: Moth's forecast distinguishes brief warm air from sustained cooling loss and marks uncertain periods.
reaction: The explicit uncertainty makes the graph more useful.
reason: Combine the forecast with the independently monitored cooler; it's the only offered combination and may complete the investigation.
expectation: The forecast and monitoring may provide a checked interpretation of the cooler's performance, without resolving every uncertainty.

effect: Rae verified the repair against independent monitoring and the old trace, completing the investigation; the supply controller's renewal warning leaves a fallback unresolved.
reaction: The warning is an intriguing complication after the reassuring service check.

mostWorthwhile.text: Independent monitoring was the most worthwhile step: it tested the repair rather than treating a running fan as proof, and left storage decisions to clinical staff.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequential repair fittings felt somewhat predictable in fast mode, although assembling the air module was satisfying.

surprise.text: Most old temperature spikes aligned with door openings, but that did not establish what every stored object experienced.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless; the later log and forecast combinations were the only offered actions, so they felt guided rather than discovered.

continue.text: Yes. The grounded repair and careful treatment of uncertainty held my interest, and the supply renewal warning makes me curious about the fallback.
